title: Marcão takes charge of Fluminense and targets Libertadores
seoTitle: Marcão takes over at Fluminense, eyes Libertadores
subtitle: The former player's composure is now the key to Tricolor's success
excerpt: Former player and assistant coach Marcão takes charge of Fluminense, aiming to secure a spot in the Copa Libertadores semifinals.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Marcão, who has previously served Fluminense as both a player and an assistant coach, takes charge of the team this season with the goal of securing a spot in the Copa Libertadores semifinals. The manager has stood out for his composure and training methods, qualities that have previously helped the club overcome difficult times.

Marcão and his journey at Fluminense

With nearly 20 years of history with the club, Marcão knows the Tricolor identity and the training ground inside out. He has already helped the team avoid relegation and secure Copa Libertadores qualification on two occasions, but was never permanently appointed as head coach. Now, the board trusts him to lead the team in decisive matches.

Record win rate and unbeaten run

In his last spell as head coach, Marcão won five matches, achieving a 73% win rate—the best in the club's history. Among the victories were matches against Palmeiras, Remo, and Vasco, while the draws came against Rivadavia and Athletico-PR.

Second leg against Platense

Fluminense arrived in Buenos Aires with a 2-0 first-leg advantage over Platense. The second leg, scheduled for 7 p.m., could seal their place in the semifinals, as a one-goal defeat would take the tie to a penalty shootout.

The role of veterans in the team

Marcão counts on experienced players like Fábio, Hulk, Thiago Silva, and Ganso, who are pillars in both attack and defense. He emphasizes the importance of listening to the veterans when drawing up the match strategy, reinforcing the idea that experience on the pitch is vital for the team.

Vision for the future and composure at the helm

The manager emphasizes that he is not thinking about a permanent promotion, but rather taking it game by game. He believes that composure and adapting to the moment are key to Fluminense's success. With the board and fans fully behind him, Marcão is prepared to lead the club to the next stage of the Libertadores.
